question.problem:
The systolic blood pressure of a group of people is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu \,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}$ and a standard deviation of $12\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}.$ Additionally, $90%$ of the people have a systolic blood pressure between $0.82\mu \,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}$ and $1.18\mu \,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}.$ Find the mean systolic blood pressure of this group, rounded to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the systolic blood pressure of a randomly selected patient. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{12}^{2}),$ and we want to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.82\mu <X<1.18\mu )=0.9.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.82\mu <X<1.18\mu ) & =0.9 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.18\mu ) & =0.9 \\ P(\mu <X<1.18\mu ) & =0.45 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.18\mu ) & =0.5+0.45 \\ P(X<1.18\mu ) & =0.95\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.18\mu ) & =0.95 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.18\mu }{12}) & =0.95 \\ Φ(\frac{0.18\mu }{12}) & =0.95 \\ \frac{0.18\mu }{12} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.95)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.95)≈1.6449.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.18\mu }{12} & =1.6449 \\ 0.18\mu  & =19.7388 \\ \mu  & =\frac{19.7388}{0.18} \\  & ≈109.66.\end{aligned}
$$
